title: Control Board Thermistor Failure
shortDescription: The electronic control board has detected a thermistor sensor failure.
fullDescription:
The F1 error on a Frigidaire microwave indicates that the electronic control board has lost communication with or detected an out-of-range reading from the temperature-sensing thermistor. The thermistor monitors cavity and component temperatures during operation.

When the reading is outside expected parameters, the control board suspends cooking operations as a safety precaution. Common triggers include a disconnected harness, a failed thermistor, or a defective control board.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the unit
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 5 minutes to reset the control board.

fixSteps.title: Inspect thermistor harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open the outer case and reseat the thermistor connector on the control board.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter to verify the thermistor reads around 10k ohms at room temperature.

whenToCallPro: Microwaves contain high-voltage capacitors that can hold lethal charge even when unplugged. Call a pro if you are not trained in discharging them.

faq.q: Can I reset the F1 code?
faq.a: Unplug for 5 minutes; if it returns, the thermistor likely needs replacement.

faq.q: Is the microwave safe to use?
faq.a: No, do not operate until the fault is cleared.

title: Touchpad or Keypad Failure
shortDescription: The control panel keypad is stuck or has shorted.
fullDescription:
F2 signals that the control board is receiving a continuous button press signal from the touchpad ribbon or one of the membrane switches is shorted. The board registers this as a stuck key and locks out operation.

Moisture intrusion, grease contamination, or physical damage to the keypad are typical causes. A failed ribbon cable or control board can also produce the same fault.

fixSteps.title: Dry the keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Let the microwave sit unplugged for 24 hours in a dry area.

fixSteps.title: Reseat touchpad ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the control panel and reconnect the flat flex cable firmly.

fixSteps.title: Replace touchpad
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new touchpad assembly if keys remain unresponsive.

whenToCallPro: If the ribbon is damaged and replacement parts are unavailable, a technician can source OEM components.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire microwave F2 stuck key fix

faq.q: Why did this happen after cleaning?
faq.a: Water often seeps behind the keypad; let it dry thoroughly.

title: Key Panel Communication Error
shortDescription: The control board cannot communicate with the key panel.
fullDescription:
F3 indicates a communication breakdown between the main control board and the keypad/display panel. The microwave cannot accept input or display menus properly.

Usually caused by a broken ribbon or a failed display module, though the main control board can also be the culprit.

fixSteps.title: Reseat all ribbon cables
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and firmly reconnect the keypad ribbon.

fixSteps.title: Replace keypad/display assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a new keypad assembly if reseating fails.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for high-voltage access.

faq.q: Is F3 the same as F2?
faq.a: F2 is a stuck key; F3 is a comms failure between modules.

title: Humidity Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The humidity sensor has failed or is disconnected.
fullDescription:
F4 means the humidity sensor used for sensor cooking is returning invalid data. The control board cannot perform auto-cook cycles that rely on humidity feedback.

Causes include a clogged or failed sensor, a detached harness, or control board issues.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor vent
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe sensor screen to remove food residue.

fixSteps.title: Reconnect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Verify sensor wiring is secure at the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace humidity sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new sensor module if readings remain invalid.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the control board needs testing.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire microwave F4 humidity sensor fix

faq.q: Can I still use the microwave?
faq.a: Manual cooking may work, but sensor modes are disabled.

title: Relay Failure
shortDescription: A relay on the control board has failed.
fullDescription:
F5 indicates a stuck or failed relay on the main control board. The relay controls power to the magnetron, turntable, or fan motor.

This typically requires control board replacement because individual relay repair is specialized work.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes and retry.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new main control board.

whenToCallPro: Recommended due to high-voltage capacitor discharge.

title: Line Voltage Frequency Error
shortDescription: AC line frequency is out of range.
fullDescription:
F6 means the control board detects an abnormal AC line frequency or a noisy power signal. The microwave will not run until voltage stabilizes.

Causes include generator-supplied power, a failing household circuit, or control board issues.

fixSteps.title: Move to dedicated outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Plug into a circuit without other appliances.

fixSteps.title: Check line voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure wall outlet voltage under load.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is clean, swap the control board.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if household voltage is out of spec.

faq.a: A line conditioner can, but basic surge strips will not.

title: Door Switch Failure
shortDescription: A door interlock switch is not detected correctly.
fullDescription:
F7 indicates the primary, secondary, or monitor door switch is sending inconsistent signals. The microwave halts operation as a safety measure since a door-open event during cooking could leak microwaves.

Door switches wear out over time and are one of the most common Frigidaire microwave failures.

fixSteps.title: Inspect door alignment
fixSteps.instruction: Check that hooks engage switches fully when closed.

fixSteps.title: Test door switches
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter in continuity mode on each switch.

fixSteps.title: Replace door switches
fixSteps.instruction: Install new primary, secondary, and monitor switches.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the door latch assembly is damaged.

faq.a: Never — bypassing door interlocks is dangerous.

title: EEPROM Checksum Error
shortDescription: The control board memory has corrupted data.
fullDescription:
F8 signals that the EEPROM on the control board failed a checksum verification. Stored settings and calibration data may be corrupt.

A firmware reset sometimes recovers the board; otherwise, replacement is required.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 15 minutes to force EEPROM re-init.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new main control board.

faq.a: Yes, replacement boards ship calibrated for the model.

title: Cooling Fan Motor Error
shortDescription: The cooling fan is not running at correct speed.
fullDescription:
F9 indicates the control board is not receiving the expected RPM feedback from the cooling fan that keeps the magnetron and electronics from overheating.

Often the fan motor has seized, the blade is blocked, or the harness is loose.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum dust and grease from the vent grilles.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Open the cabinet and spin the fan blade by hand.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new cooling fan motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro to discharge the HV capacitor before work.
videoSearchQuery: Frigidaire microwave F9 cooling fan fix

faq.q: Why does the unit shut down?
faq.a: Thermal protection engages when the magnetron overheats.

title: Analog-to-Digital Converter Failure
shortDescription: The control board ADC circuit has failed.
fullDescription:
F10 indicates the analog-to-digital converter on the main control board is returning invalid data. The board cannot interpret sensor readings, so cooking is disabled.

This is almost always a control board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Dry the board
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and let dry 24 hours if moisture is suspected.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new main control board.

faq.a: Not economically; replacement is the standard fix.
